headline: Manage Seasonal Camping Permits and Water Access
reservation: Park entry is free, but seasonal camping byelaws apply from March to September. During this period, you must secure a permit or book a formal campsite in specific lochshore areas; check the official Loch Lomond & The Trossachs website for the latest Management Byelaws review updates.

days.title: Highland Boundary Discovery

stops.name: Conic Hill
stops.detail: View the Highland Boundary Fault line where the lowlands and highlands meet over Loch Lomond.

stops.name: Inchcailloch
stops.detail: Take a waterbus to this island to see ancient woodlands and diverse wildlife.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour; use the National Park Journey Planner for local waterbus connections.
days.note: Pacing at Conic Hill is a suggestion; trails can be steep and busy at mid-day.

days.title: Trossachs Lochs and Glens

stops.name: Duke's Pass
stops.detail: Drive or cycle this famous winding route through the wooded hills of The Trossachs.

stops.name: Loch Katrine
stops.detail: Cruise the waters that inspired famous poets or stroll along the tranquil shore.

days.driving: Allow 1.5 hours; conditions vary on narrow wooded roads.
days.note: Check steamship or cruise schedules in advance as they operate seasonally.

days.title: Peaks of Breadalbane

stops.name: Ben More
stops.detail: Challenge yourself on the highest Munro in the park, standing at 1174m.

stops.name: Falls of Dochart
stops.detail: Observe the tumbling white water in the village of Killin.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour; A82 traffic can be heavy during peak travel times.
days.note: Munro bagging requires significant time; allow a full day for Ben More and check weather forecasts.

intel.title: Gateway and Trailhead Hubs
intel.text: Major car parks are located at Balloch, Luss, and Tarbet. Use the National Park Journey Planner app to locate electric vehicle charging points and check site availability.

intel.title: Network and Apps
intel.text: Internet signal varies greatly between lowland towns and highland glens. Official audio guides for rail routes are available via mobile apps, but download them before departing Glasgow or Edinburgh.

intel.title: Corridor Supply Points
intel.text: Fuel is accessible along the A82 at Balloch and Tyndrum. Distances between stations increase in the northern Breadalbane area; check vehicle levels before entering remote glens.

intel.title: Seasonal Byelaws
intel.text: Camping restrictions are strictly enforced between March and September. Autumn brings dramatic leaf changes, while winter maintenance can affect local trail access.

intel.title: Water and Rail Links
intel.text: The West Highland Line provides scenic access to stations like Arrochar & Tarbet. Waterbus services connect eastern and western shores, but schedules are weather-dependent.

plan.arrival: Pick up rentals at Glasgow Airport, then follow the M8 and A82 to Balloch. Stock up on supplies in Balloch, the 'gateway to the west', before heading deeper into the park.
plan.vehicle: Campervans are popular but must follow specific parking and overnight permit rules; check road restrictions for narrow glens.
plan.goldenHour: Sunset over Loch Lomond from Conic Hill provides a classic view of the fault line islands.

sources.label: Loch Lomond & The Trossachs National Park Authority
